svg.title: Shell-and-tube heat exchanger — two-pass U-tube section
svg.desc: Four hollow U-tubes return the cold stream from the lower channel chamber to the upper outlet. A sealed divider separates the two channel chambers. The hot shell-side stream enters at the upper left, passes through alternating segmental-baffle windows, and leaves at the lower right. Hatched walls and tube sheet show sectioned metal; arrowheads distinguish the two fluid circuits without mixing them. The assembled view shows the same unit from outside: shell, bolted girth flange with the tube-sheet rim, channel bonnet, nozzles and saddles. Probe layer (hidden at rest): pointing along the section places a thermocouple traverse at that station and reads the shell and both tube-pass temperatures from the 1-2 exchanger model - shell fluid mixed over each cross-section, plug flow in each pass, constant U, U-bend area not counted - for hot in 150 °C, cold in 30 °C, Cc/Ch = 0.8, UA/Cc = 1.5: hot out 95.5 °C, cold out 98.2 °C, F = 0.78. Arrows give the local heat-flow direction; past x/L = 0.93 the upper pass is hotter than the shell and returns heat to it. Below the section, a temperature profile from the same model: shell T and both tube passes against x/L (axis aligned with the straight tube length), the cross marked; while probing, a cursor follows the station.
